_method: Shortlist = episodes whose named actors appear anywhere in Livy 41-45 (EN). This is a RETRIEVAL step; a shortlisted episode is NOT evidence of access — most actors (Perseus, Paullus, Eumenes) are fully covered by Plutarch's Aemilius Paullus, Polybius, and the Periochae. The test fails only if an episode's specific CONTENT is unique to 41-45.

shortlist.episode: The people rose against the insolent nobility, forcing the creation of the tribunes of the plebs, which stabilized the republic by giving all three forms their share.
shortlist.quote: E così nacque la creazione de’ Tribuni della plebe, dopo la quale creazione venne a essere più stabilito lo stato di que

shortlist.episode: Once the Tarquins were dead and the nobles' fear gone, the nobility spat out against the plebs the venom it had held in its breast.
shortlist.quote: come prima ei furono morti i Tarquinii, e che ai Nobili fu la paura fuggita, cominciarono a sputare contro alla Plebe qu

shortlist.episode: After confusions, uproars, and dangers of scandal between plebs and nobility, the tribunes were created for the security of the plebs.
shortlist.quote: si venne, per sicurtà della Plebe, alla creazione de’ Tribuni; e quelli ordinarono con tante preminenzie e tanta riputaz

shortlist.episode: From the Tarquins to the Gracchi, more than three hundred years, Rome's tumults rarely produced exile and most rarely blood.
shortlist.quote: da’ Tarquinii ai Gracchi, che furano più di trecento anni, i tumulti di Roma rade volte partorivano esilio e radissime s

shortlist.episode: Coriolanus, enemy of the popular faction, advised starving the plebs to strip the tribunes' authority, and only the tribunes' formal citation saved him from being killed by the mob.
shortlist.quote: Coriolano, inimico alla fazione popolare, consigliò come egli era venuto il tempo da potere gastigare la Plebe

shortlist.episode: Manlius Capitolinus, envious of Camillus' glory, calumniated the nobles over the Gallic treasure before the plebs, and the dictator, when Manlius could produce no particulars, had him imprisoned.
shortlist.quote: Manlio Capitolino non poteva sopportare che gli fusse attribuito tanto onore e tanta gloria

shortlist.episode: Caesar, founder of Rome's tyranny, is celebrated only because writers were corrupted by his fortune; free writers blame him through Catiline and praise his enemy Brutus.
shortlist.quote: Né sia alcuno che s’inganni, per la gloria di Cesare, sentendolo, massime, celebrare dagli scrittori

shortlist.episode: Of the twenty-six emperors from Caesar to Maximinus sixteen were killed; the good adoptive emperors from Nerva to Marcus lived secure while Caligula, Nero, and Vitellius could not be saved by their armies.
shortlist.quote: di ventisei imperadori che furono da Cesare a Massimino, sedici ne furono ammazzati, dieci morirono ordinariamente

shortlist.episode: After plague, famine, and prodigies, the nobles claimed the gods were angry at the plebeian tribunes with consular power, and the frightened plebs elected tribunes who were all nobles.
shortlist.quote: la plebe, sbigottita da questa religione, creò i Tribuni tutti nobili

shortlist.episode: During the long siege of Veii, oracles tied victory to draining the swollen Alban lake, which kept the weary soldiers at the siege until Camillus as dictator took the city.
shortlist.quote: essendo il lago Albano, quello anno, cresciuto mirabilmente, ed essendo i soldati romani infastiditi per la lunga ossidi

shortlist.episode: Against the Terentillan law the nobility had the Sibylline books consulted, which warned that civil sedition threatened the city's liberty that year, cooling the plebs.
shortlist.quote: fecero vedere i libri Sibillini, e rispondere come alla città, mediante la civile sedizione, soprastavano quello anno pe

shortlist.episode: Appius Herdonius with four thousand exiles and slaves seized the Capitol by night, and Publius Ruberius induced the plebs to swear obedience to the consul and retake it.
shortlist.quote: avendo un Appio Erdonio, con una moltitudine di sbanditi e di servi, in numero di quattromila uomini, occupato di notte

shortlist.episode: The new consul Titus Quinctius held the plebs to its oath to the dead consul, and out of fear of religion the plebs obeyed the consul rather than believe the tribunes.
shortlist.quote: Tito Livio mostra come la Plebe, per paura della religione, volle più tosto ubbidire al consolo, che credere a’ tribuni

shortlist.episode: Papirius, encouraging his soldiers against the Samnite linen legion drawn up near Aquilonia, said crests make no wounds and the Roman pilum passes through painted and gilded shields, and the Samnites were defeated.
shortlist.quote: Contro a costoro venne Papirio; il quale, nel confortare i suoi soldati, disse: «non enim cristas vulnera facere, et pic

shortlist.episode: The sons of Brutus, with other Roman youths, conspired against the fatherland because under the consuls they could no longer profit extraordinarily as under the kings, and were executed.
shortlist.quote: non furono indotti, insieme con altri giovani romani, a congiurare contro alla patria per altro, se non perché non si po

shortlist.episode: Rome, having expelled the Tarquins while still uncorrupted, could immediately take and maintain its liberty, an oath against kings sufficing to keep the people firm.
shortlist.quote: la quale, cacciati i Tarquinii, poté subito prendere e mantenere quella libertà

shortlist.episode: After the deaths of Caesar, Caligula, and Nero and the extinction of the whole Caesarean line, corrupted Rome could not even begin to recover liberty.
shortlist.quote: morto Cesare, morto Caio Caligola, morto Nerone, spenta tutta la stirpe cesarea, non poté mai, non solamente mantenere,

shortlist.episode: The corruption that the Marian factions, headed by Caesar, had introduced into the Roman people so blinded the multitude that it did not see the yoke it was placing on its own neck.
shortlist.quote: quella corruzione che le parti mariane avevano messa nel popolo; delle quali sendo capo Cesare, potette accecare quella

shortlist.episode: Despite the difficulty of Hannibal's Alpine and Apennine crossings, the Romans chose to await him first at the Ticinus and then on the plain of Arezzo rather than destroy their army in harsh mountain positions.
shortlist.quote: i Romani l’aspettarono prima in sul Tesino, e dipoi nel piano d’Arezzo

shortlist.episode: Mucius Scaevola burned the hand that had erred in trying to kill Porsenna, king of the Tuscans, and received the same public reward of land.
shortlist.quote: l’altro si arse la mano, che aveva errato, volendo ammazzare Porsenna, re degli Toscani

shortlist.episode: Manlius Capitolinus, rewarded with a small measure of flour for saving the Capitol from the besieging Gauls, was later thrown headlong from that same Capitol when he stirred sedition in Rome, without regard for his merits.
shortlist.quote: per avere salvato il Campidoglio da’ Franciosi che vi erano a campo

shortlist.episode: Rome's ingratitude toward Scipio arose from a suspicion born of the greatness of his victory over Carthage and his extraordinary reputation, with Cato Priscus the first to move against him.
shortlist.quote: la ingratitudine usata a Scipione nacque da uno sospetto che i cittadini cominciarono avere di lui

shortlist.episode: Coriolanus and Camillus were exiled for injuries each had done to the plebs; Coriolanus was never pardoned, while Camillus was recalled and adored like a prince for the rest of his life.
shortlist.quote: Coriolano e Cammillo furono fatti esuli per ingiuria che l’uno e l’altro avea fatto alla plebe

shortlist.episode: Sergius and Verginius, each commanding part of the army besieging Veii, refused out of rivalry to aid one another and were punished only with fines rather than death.
shortlist.quote: Erano Sergio e Virginio a campo a Veio, ciascuno preposto a una parte dello esercito

shortlist.episode: When the dictator Papirius Cursor wanted to execute Fabius for fighting the Samnites against his orders, Fabius' father argued that the Roman people had never so treated even defeated commanders.
shortlist.quote: Quando Papirio Cursore voleva fare morire Fabio, per avere, contro al suo comandamento, combattuto co’ Sanniti

shortlist.episode: Caesar's virtue, first favored by Pompey and others, turned into a source of fear too late, and the remedies attempted against him accelerated the ruin of the Roman republic.
shortlist.quote: Pompeio aveva tardi cominciato a temere Cesare

shortlist.episode: The agrarian law lay dormant until the Gracchi reawakened it, finding its opponents' power doubled, kindling such hatred between plebs and Senate that it came to arms and blood.
shortlist.quote: questa legge stette come addormentata infino ai Gracchi; da’ quali essendo poi svegliata, rovinò al tutto la libertà rom

shortlist.episode: The plebs made Marius consul four times and the nobility, lacking other remedy, raised up Sulla as head of its party, leading to civil wars won by the nobility.
shortlist.quote: e volse la sua riputazione a Mario tanto che la lo fece quattro volte consule

shortlist.episode: The same humors revived with Caesar heading Marius' party and Pompey Sulla's; Caesar prevailed and became Rome's first tyrant, so the city was never free again.
shortlist.quote: fattosi Cesare capo della parte di Mario, e Pompeio di quella di Silla, venendo alle mani, rimase superiore Cesare

shortlist.episode: During a grave pestilence in Rome, the Volsci and Aequi attacked the Latins and Hernici, and the Senate, unable to defend them, authorized them to arm and defend themselves.
shortlist.quote: risposero che pigliassero partito di difendersi da loro medesimi e con le loro armi

shortlist.episode: The second Decemvirate showed its pride, beating plebs and Senate alike, and to terrify them increased the lictors from twelve to one hundred twenty.
shortlist.quote: in cambio di dodici littori, ne feciono cento venti

shortlist.episode: War moved by the Sabines and Volsci forced the Ten to convene the Senate, where Valerius and Horatius spoke against their pride.
shortlist.quote: i Sabini ed i Volsci mossero guerra a’ Romani

shortlist.episode: Appius, having skillfully simulated popularity to win the plebs and secure his reappointment, suddenly changed nature, showing himself the plebs' enemy, proud instead of humane, so that everyone saw his deceit.
shortlist.quote: mutare, in uno subito, natura; e, di amico, mostrarsi inimico alla plebe; di umano, superbo

shortlist.episode: The plebs demanded of Valerius and Horatius the restoration of tribunes and appeal, but also that the Ten be handed over to be burned alive, which the envoys condemned as impious.
shortlist.quote: che si dessono loro tutti i Dieci che gli volevono ardere vivi

shortlist.episode: After Cannae, Pacuvius Calavius in Capua reconciled the plebs with the Senate by locking up the senators and inviting the people to replace each one, whereupon the people found every proposed substitute unworthy.
shortlist.quote: trovandosi in quel tempo nel supremo magistrato Pacuvio Calano, e conoscendo il pericolo che portava quella città di tum

shortlist.episode: Rome created the censors to guard its morals, first for five-year terms; the dictator Mamercus by a new law reduced the office to eighteen months, and the offended censors expelled him from the Senate without remedy.
shortlist.quote: fu corretto dalla prudenza di Mamerco dittatore, il quale per nuova legge ridusse detto magistrato a diciotto mesi

shortlist.episode: Fabius Maximus could not persuade the Roman people that proceeding slowly against Hannibal was useful, since the people judged that course cowardly, and his master of horse was given authority to fight.
shortlist.quote: non poteva persuadere al Popolo romano, che fusse utile a quella Republica procedere lentamente in quella guerra, e sost

shortlist.episode: Varro was made consul only for having promised in all the public places of Rome to crush Hannibal, from which followed the battle and rout of Cannae and almost the ruin of Rome.
shortlist.quote: fece di poi consule Varrone, non per altri suoi meriti che per avere, per tutte le piazze e tutti i luoghi publici di Ro

shortlist.episode: Marcus Centenius Penula, a most vile man, obtained from the wary Senate authority to raise volunteers against Hannibal and was routed and killed with all his followers.
shortlist.quote: venne in Senato Marco Centenio Penula, uomo vilissimo (nondimanco aveva avuto qualche grado nella milizia)

shortlist.episode: Scipio, made consul and desiring the province of Africa while promising Carthage's ruin, threatened to take the proposal to the people when the Senate balked on Fabius Maximus' advice.
shortlist.quote: Scipione, quando fu fatto consolo, e che desiderava la provincia di Africa, promettendo al tutto la rovina di Cartagine

shortlist.episode: To satisfy Camillus' vow of a tenth of the Veientine spoils to Apollo, the Senate issued an edict that each man present publicly a tenth of his plunder, trusting wholly in the plebs' goodness.
shortlist.quote: fece il Senato uno editto, che ciascuno dovessi rappresentare in publico la decima parte di quello ch’egli aveva predato

shortlist.episode: Before the Gauls came to Rome, the plebeian Marcus Caedicius reported to the Senate that at midnight on the Via Nuova he had heard a more-than-human voice warning that the Gauls were coming.
shortlist.quote: uno Marco Cedicio plebeio riferì al Senato avere udito di mezza notte, passando per la Via nuova, una voce, maggiore che

shortlist.episode: Cities where peoples rule make excessive gains in a very short time, as Rome did after the expulsion of the kings and Athens after freeing itself from Pisistratus.
shortlist.quote: come fece Roma dopo la cacciata de’ re, ed Atene da poi che la si liberò da Pisistrato

shortlist.episode: Pompey, routed by Caesar in Thessaly, fled to Egypt to Ptolemy, whom he had previously restored to his kingdom, and was killed by him.
shortlist.quote: Pompeio, rotto che fu da Cesare in Tessaglia, si rifuggì in Egitto a Tolomeo, il quale era per lo adietro da lui stato r

shortlist.episode: Valerius Corvinus was made consul at twenty-three, and told his soldiers that the consulate was the reward of virtue, not of blood.
shortlist.quote: si vede per il testimone di Valerio Corvino, che fu fatto Consolo in ventitré anni

shortlist.episode: Rome availed itself of Valerius Corvinus, Scipio, Pompey, and many others who triumphed very young.
shortlist.quote: come si valse Roma di Valerio Corvino, di Scipione e di Pompeio, e di molti altri, che trionfarono giovanissimi

shortlist.episode: The sequence of Rome's wars: first the Aequi and Volsci, then the Samnites, the Latin revolt (with Samnite help for Rome), the Tuscans, Pyrrhus, and finally Carthage, never two great wars at once.
shortlist.quote: mentre che combatterno con gli Equi e con i Volsci, mai, mentre che questi popoli furono potenti, non scesero contro di

shortlist.episode: After the First Punic War all the Gauls on both sides of the Alps conspired against Rome and were slaughtered between Populonia and Pisa.
shortlist.quote: intra Populonia e Pisa, dove è oggi la torre a San Vincenti, furono con massima strage superati

shortlist.episode: The Carthaginians, powerful but distant, never thought of attacking Rome or aiding the Samnites and Tuscans, even seeking Roman friendship until it was too late.
shortlist.quote: fece che non pensarono mai di assaltare quello, né di soccorrere i Sanniti ed i Toscani

shortlist.episode: Rome entered provinces through local friends: the Capuans into Samnium, Camertines in Tuscany, Mamertines in Sicily, Saguntines in Spain, Masinissa in Africa, Aetolians in Greece.
shortlist.quote: per il mezzo de’ Capuani entrarono in Sannio, de’ Camertini in Toscana, de’ Mamertini in Sicilia, de’ Saguntini in Spagn

shortlist.episode: The Samnites, while free, resisted Rome for forty-six years until the consulship of Papirius Cursor the younger despite repeated defeats.
shortlist.quote: potessono infino al tempo di Papirio Cursore consolo, figliuolo del primo Papirio, resistere a’ Romani

shortlist.episode: Reduced to servitude, the Samnites sent envoys begging Hannibal for help because they could barely defend themselves against one Roman legion at Nola.
shortlist.quote: sendo i Sanniti oppressi da una legione di uomini che era in Nola, mandarono oratori ad Annibale, a pregarlo che gli soc

shortlist.episode: All Roman wars from the city's beginning to the siege of Veii — against Latins, Samnites and Tuscans — were dispatched in six, ten or twenty days by immediate pitched battle.
shortlist.quote: tutte si vedranno ispedite, quale in sei, quale in dieci, quale in venti dì

shortlist.episode: The first of Rome's three migration wars: the capture of Rome by the Gauls who had earlier seized Lombardy.
shortlist.quote: La prima fu quella quando Roma fu presa, la quale fu occupata da quei Franciosi che avevano tolto, come di sopra si diss

shortlist.episode: The second: after the First Punic War the Romans killed more than two hundred thousand Gauls between Piombino and Pisa.
shortlist.quote: quella che fecero dopo la prima guerra cartaginese, quando intra Piombino e Pisa ammazzarono più che dugentomila Francio

shortlist.episode: The Samnite war arose by chance when the oppressed Campanians gave themselves to Rome, forcing the Romans to defend them as subjects against their Samnite allies.
shortlist.quote: sendo i Campani oppressati, e ricorrendo a Roma fuora della opinione de’ Romani e de’ Sanniti, furono forzati, dandosi i

shortlist.episode: The First Punic War likewise began by chance from Rome's defense of the Messinesi in Sicily.
shortlist.quote: Questa medesima cagione dette principio alla prima guerra contro ai Cartaginesi, per la defensione che i Romani presono

shortlist.episode: Hannibal attacked Rome's Saguntine friends in Spain not to harm them but to provoke Roman arms and gain occasion to pass into Italy.
shortlist.quote: Annibale capitano cartaginese assaltò i Saguntini amici de’ Romani in Ispagna, non per offendere quelli, ma per muovere

shortlist.episode: Livy, debating whether Alexander would have beaten Rome, names three necessities of war — many good soldiers, prudent captains and good fortune — never mentioning money.
shortlist.quote: mostra essere tre cose necessarie nella guerra; assai soldati e buoni, capitani prudenti, e buona fortuna

shortlist.episode: The Capuans, measuring their power by money rather than soldiers, aided the Sidicini and after two defeats had to make themselves tributaries of Rome.
shortlist.quote: preso ch’egli ebbero partito di aiutargli, dopo due rotte furono constretti farsi tributari de’ Romani, se si vollono sa

shortlist.episode: Hasdrubal, caught in the Marches by Claudius Nero and the other consul, had to choose between flight and battle, and chose battle.
shortlist.quote: come intervenne a Asdrubale, quando nella Marca fu assaltato da Claudio Nerone, insieme con l’altro console romano

shortlist.episode: The Tarentine ambassadors demanded peace between Rome and the Samnites; the Roman consul, laughing, had battle sounded in their presence.
shortlist.quote: il Console, ridendosi di questa proposta, alla presenza di detti ambasciadori fece sonare a battaglia

shortlist.episode: Scipio attacked Africa to lift the war from Italy.
shortlist.quote: Allega Scipione che, per levare la guerra di Italia, assaltò la Africa

shortlist.episode: Rome's greatest early fraud was making 'companions' of the Latins and neighbors, who under that name made themselves slaves with their own arms and blood.
shortlist.quote: Né poté usare, nel principio, il maggiore inganno, che pigliare il modo, discorso di sopra da noi, di farsi compagni; pe

shortlist.episode: The Latins recognized the deception only after Rome's double defeat of the Samnites, as the Latin praetor Annius Setinus declared in their council.
shortlist.quote: «Nam si etiam nunc sub umbra foederis aequi servitutem pati possumus etc.»

shortlist.episode: When the Samnites complained of Latin attacks, Rome, not wishing to irritate the Latins, declined to forbid the war — which emboldened the Latins and made them open enemies sooner, as Annius's speech on Roman patience shows.
shortlist.quote: i Romani non vollono proibire ai Latini tale guerra, disiderando non gli irritare: il che non solamente non gli irritò m

shortlist.episode: In the Latin council the praetor Annius urged deciding what to do rather than what to say, since words are easily fitted once plans are unfolded.
shortlist.quote: Ad summam rerum nostrarum pertinere arbitror, ut cogitetis magis, quid agendum nobis, quam quid loquendum sit

shortlist.episode: The Lavinians delayed aiding the Latins so long that as they marched out the gate news came of the Latin defeat, prompting the praetor Milionius's remark that the short march would cost them dear with Rome.
shortlist.quote: Questo poco della via ci costerà assai col Popolo romano

shortlist.episode: Rome's most important battle ever, against the Latins in the consulship of Torquatus and Decius, with armies equal in order, virtue, obstinacy and number, Livy giving the edge only to the Roman commanders; Livy's account also sets out the hastati-principes-triarii order.
shortlist.quote: fu questa che ei fece con i popoli latini, nel consolato di Torquato e di Decio

shortlist.episode: To hold their soldiers firm and resolved, one consul killed himself (Decius's devotio) and the other his own son (Torquatus).
shortlist.quote: di due Consoli, per tenere fermi gli animi de’ soldati, ed ubbidienti a’ comandamenti loro, e diliberati al combattere l

shortlist.episode: At Lake Regillus the Romans, their army wavering against the Latins, dismounted their cavalry to fight on foot, renewed the battle and won.
shortlist.quote: quando si azzuffarono con i Latini appresso al lago Regillo; dove essendo già inclinato lo esercito romano

shortlist.episode: At Cannae Hannibal mocked the Roman consuls for making their cavalry dismount, saying he would rather have them delivered to him bound.
shortlist.quote: veggendo in la giornata di Canne che i Consoli avevano fatto discendere a piè li loro cavalieri

shortlist.episode: Crassus and Mark Antony marched for days through Parthian territory with much infantry and few horse against innumerable Parthian cavalry; Antony saved himself, Crassus was deceived rather than overpowered.
shortlist.quote: Crasso e Marc’Antonio romani corsono per il dominio de’ Parti molte giornate con pochissimi cavagli ed assai fanteria

shortlist.episode: Marcus Atilius Regulus presumed to withstand not only cavalry but elephants with his infantry, trusting in its virtue even though the design failed.
shortlist.quote: Presunse Marco Regolo Attilio, non solo con la fanteria sua sostenere i cavagli, ma gli elefanti

shortlist.episode: The acquisition of Capua, a city of delights, corrupted first Rome's soldiers and later Hannibal's army, as Livy attests.
shortlist.quote: come intervenne a Roma, prima, nello acquisto di Capova, e dipoi, a Annibale

shortlist.episode: Two Roman legions left to protect Capua grew corrupt in idleness and plotted to seize the country they had defended, a conspiracy Rome suppressed.
shortlist.quote: lasciarono due legioni nel paese di Capova, che gli difendesse. Le quali legioni marcendo nell’ozio, cominciarono a dile

shortlist.episode: The people of Rhegium were deprived of life and city by the legion the Romans had placed there as a garrison.
shortlist.quote: quello de’ Regini, a’ quali fu tolto la vita e la terra da una legione che i Romani vi avevano messa in guardia

shortlist.episode: After the Romans defeated the Latins, the praetor Numicius proclaimed through Latium that the weakened Romans could now be attacked; the peoples who believed him raised a new army and were promptly routed.
shortlist.quote: il quale, vinto che i Romani ebbero i Latini, gridava per tutto il paese di Lazio, che allora era tempo assaltare i Roma

shortlist.episode: On Camillus's proposal the Senate judged the defeated Latins town by town, either benefiting each with citizenship and privileges or destroying it, never taking the neutral course.
shortlist.quote: recatosi innanzi, terra per terra, tutti quegli ch’erano di momento, o e’ gli benificarono o e’ gli spensono

shortlist.episode: The Latins were conquered and utterly crushed, first by Manlius Torquatus and then by Camillus, who garrisoned all Latium and took hostages.
shortlist.quote: Erano, dunque, vinti i Latini ed al tutto afflitti, prima da Manlio Torquato, e dipoi da Cammillo

shortlist.episode: The Samnites at the Caudine Forks rejected the old man's advice to free the Romans honorably or kill them all, and by the middle way—disarming and humiliating them—earned their own ruin.
shortlist.quote: come la fu ai Sanniti quando avevano rinchiusi i Romani alle Forche Gaudine

shortlist.episode: Tarentum was recovered only when Fabius Maximus was sent a year later with a whole army—which could have retaken it even without the citadel.
shortlist.quote: alla ricuperazione di Taranto, in capo di uno anno, fu mandato Fabio Massimo con tutto lo esercito

shortlist.episode: After Valerius Corvinus quieted the sedition born of the Capua legions' conspiracy, the settlement imposed the gravest penalties on anyone who reproached the soldiers with that sedition.
shortlist.quote: essendone di questa congiura nata una sedizione, la quale fu poi da Valerio Corvino quietata

shortlist.episode: Tiberius Gracchus, commanding slaves armed in the war against Hannibal, made it a capital offense for anyone to reproach any of them with their servitude.
shortlist.quote: Tiberio Gracco, fatto, nella guerra di Annibale, capitano sopra certo numero di servi che i Romani, per carestia d’uomin

shortlist.episode: After Cannae, Hanno counseled Carthage to use the victory wisely by making peace with Rome on honorable terms; the advice was rejected and later recognized as wise when the occasion was lost.
shortlist.quote: Consigliava Annone, uno vecchio e prudente cittadino cartaginese, che si usasse questa vittoria saviamente in fare pace

shortlist.episode: Hannibal, recalled to save Carthage, did not blush to ask for peace before risking his country's last stake in battle, and only fought when peace was denied.
shortlist.quote: non si vergognò di domandare la pace, giudicando, se alcuno rimedio aveva la sua patria, era in quella e non nella guerr

shortlist.episode: The three Fabii, sent as envoys to the Gauls attacking Chiusi, fought against them contrary to the law of nations; instead of being surrendered or punished they were made tribunes, and the enraged Gauls took Rome except the Capitol.
shortlist.quote: ei mandarono i tre Fabii oratori a’ Franciosi, che erano venuti a assaltare la Toscana, ed in particulare Chiusi

shortlist.episode: Heaven made the Fabii envoys err and provoke the Gauls to war, had Camillus exiled to Ardea, prevented the naming of a dictator, and let Rome prepare feebly against the Gallic assault.
shortlist.quote: fece prima errare quegli Fabii che andarono oratori a’ Franciosi, e, mediante l’opera loro, gli concitò a fare guerra a

shortlist.episode: The Romans, slow to arms, met the Gauls on the river Allia ten miles from Rome with a carelessly placed camp and thin ranks, and fled almost without bloodshed.
shortlist.quote: furono tanto pigri al pigliare l’arme, che a fatica furono a tempo a scontrare i Franciosi sopra il fiume di Allia, disc

shortlist.episode: Fortune, wishing to beat Rome but not destroy it, preserved the Capitol and prepared the recovery, keeping an intact Roman army at Veii and Camillus untainted at Ardea.
shortlist.quote: avendo condotto uno esercito romano intero a Veio, e Cammillo a Ardea, da potere fare grossa testa

shortlist.episode: The Romans besieged on the Capitol were about to ransom themselves with gold from the Gauls when Camillus arrived with his army as the gold was being weighed, so that Rome was not redeemed by gold.
shortlist.quote: sopra tale convenzione pesandosi di già l’oro, sopravvenne Cammillo con lo esercito suo

shortlist.episode: The Massilians, Aedui, Rhodians, Hiero of Syracuse, kings Eumenes and Masinissa, all neighbors of Roman empire, contributed expenses and tribute for Rome's friendship, asking only protection.
shortlist.quote: i Massiliensi, gli Edui, i Rodiani, Ierone siracusano, Eumene e Massinissa regi, i quali tutti erano vicini ai confini d

shortlist.episode: After Hannibal's coming into Italy and three defeats, Rome, its heart well armed, could still sustain the enemy and win the war through the people of Rome, the Latin name, allied towns and colonies.

verdict: NO HIT: zero episodes with content uniquely attested in Livy 41-45

expert_assessment.method: manual review of all 133 shortlisted episodes against the question: does the episode's specific content require Livy 41-45, or is it derivable from books Machiavelli had (1-10, 21-40), the Periochae, or non-Livian sources?
findings: The overwhelming majority of shortlisted episodes anchor to books 1-10 and 21-30 (actor-name retrieval over-matches: 'Plebe', 'Gauls', 'Camillus', 'Hannibal' appear throughout Livy).

Era-of-41-45 candidates examined: (a) disc:it:2:30 Rhodians/Eumenes/Masinissa as gift-bound friends — generic diplomatic knowledge, fully present in Polybian tradition and the Periochae; no narrative detail specific to 41-45. (b) The Perseus-stinginess material in the money-is-not-the-sinews-of-war discussion (disc II.10) — the refused Gallic mercenaries episode is in Livy 44 BUT is equally and more vividly in Plutarch, Aemilius Paullus 12-13, a source Machiavelli demonstrably used; no 41-45-specific detail (names, figures, sequence) appears. (c) Imperial-era actors (Tiberius, Commodus, Severus in III.6) are from Tacitus/Herodian/Dio tradition, irrelevant to Livy access.
No episode reproduces content (names, numbers, episode structure) attested ONLY in 41-45.
expert_assessment.conclusion: Consistent with the documented recovery history: Machiavelli wrote without Books 41-45. The access story stands. Assessment is expert-judgment over a machine shortlist; records: this file.
